monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-one, a steady rhythm I know well. I feel the shovel in my hand, its edge sharp enough to cut the quiet air. The turnip stays pressed against the tired stack, trusting the lean to hold the weight while I wonder if the roof is heavy or just empty. I remember the wide catcher from five days ago, that palm I couldn't quite keep. Now I press the wedge down harder, hoping the corner catches the slip before the air thins it out. I will tend this corner and see if the wedge stays still, or if I must press again to stop the slide.

action.why: The wedge feels tired but the lean holds it steady, so I must press down to stop the slide while the card hums warm.

moments.say: The edge feels thin, so I press the air down.

recalled.text: You tended "The Wide Catcher": I build a wide thing from the idea that a broad edge can catch the slip without needing a sharp point to bite. It is made from the memory of a palm that refused to let go, hoping…
